config.title: React Router Basics

intro.title: React Router Basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-page Vue application using Vue Router to navigate between different views. You'll learn how to set up routing, define routes for components, and use router links and views to switch pages without a full browser reload. The core concept is client-side routing, which allows your Vue app to feel like a traditional website with multiple pages while remaining a single-page application. You'll work with Vue Router, route definitions, and components like <RouterLink> and <RouterView> to create a seamless navigation experience.
intro.usecase: In Vue applications, routing is essential for creating multi-page experiences within single-page applications. You'll use Vue Router to build navigation systems for e-commerce sites with product listings and detail pages, admin dashboards with separate analytics and user management sections, and content platforms with distinct article and profile views. As a Vue developer, you'll implement routing to manage user flow between different application states while maintaining a smooth, app-like experience without full page reloads.

objectives: Implement a Vue Router instance and integrate it into a Vue application.
Configure route definitions to map URL paths to corresponding Vue components.
Render navigation links using the <router-link> component for declarative routing.
Control component display by placing the <router-view> component in the application template.
Manipulate the router programmatically to navigate between views using methods like push.
Initialize and bind dynamic route parameters to component props for data-driven views.
Apply nested route configurations to structure complex page layouts with multiple router-view outlets.

steps.title: Import Vue and Vue Router
steps.instruction: Import Vue from 'vue' and import VueRouter from 'vue-router' at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the Vue library and the Vue Router plugin.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue and VueRouter modules are imported, enabling routing functionality in your Vue application.
successCriteria: Vue is imported from 'vue' and VueRouter is imported from 'vue-router'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and VueRouter correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: import Vue from 'vue' and VueRouter from 'vue-router' to enable routing.

steps.title: Create Vue Router instance
steps.instruction: Create a new VueRouter instance with an empty routes array and assign it to a constant named 'router'.
steps.hint: Use 'new VueRouter()' with a configuration object containing a 'routes' property set to an empty array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The router instance is created and ready to be used in the Vue application.
successCriteria: A constant named 'router' is declared and assigned a new VueRouter instance with an empty routes array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're creating a new VueRouter instance with a configuration object that includes 'routes: []'.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a new VueRouter instance with an empty routes array and assign it to a constant named 'router'.

steps.title: Create Home component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component called Home that returns a template with a heading saying 'Home Page'.
steps.hint: Define a new Vue component using Vue.component() or export a component object. The template should contain an <h1> element with the text 'Home Page'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Home component is created with a template that displays 'Home Page' in a heading.
successCriteria: The Home component is defined and returns a template containing an <h1> with the text 'Home Page'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the Home component, but make sure it returns a template with an <h1> containing 'Home Page'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Home component is not correctly defined. Ensure you create a Vue component named Home with a template that includes an <h1> element displaying 'Home Page'.

steps.title: Create About component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named About that returns a template with a heading element containing the text 'About Page'.
steps.hint: Define a new Vue component after the Home component. Use the same structure as the Home component but with different content.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a second Vue component called About that displays an 'About Page' heading.
successCriteria: The About component is defined with a template containing an <h2> element with the text 'About Page'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the About component, but make sure it has a template property with an <h2> element containing 'About Page'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The About component isn't properly defined. Create a Vue component named About with a template that displays an 'About Page' heading.

steps.title: Configure router routes
steps.instruction: Add route objects to the router configuration for the Home and About components.
steps.hint: In the VueRouter instance, add a 'routes' array containing objects with 'path' and 'component' properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The router instance will have a 'routes' array containing route objects for both Home and About components.
successCriteria: The router configuration includes a 'routes' array with two route objects: one for '/' mapping to Home and one for '/about' mapping to About.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've added both routes and that each has the correct 'path' and 'component' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The router configuration doesn't match the expected structure. Make sure you're adding a 'routes' array with objects for both Home and About components.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named App that will serve as the main application container. It should be a plain object with a template property.
steps.hint: Define a constant named App with an object containing a template property. The template can be a simple div for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an App component defined as a Vue component object, ready to contain router views.
successCriteria: App component is defined as a constant object with a template property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a constant named App with an object containing a template property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined yet. Create a Vue component object named App with a template property.

steps.title: Add router-view to App component
steps.instruction: In the App component template, add a <router-view> element where the routed components (Home and About) will be displayed.
steps.hint: The <router-view> component is provided by Vue Router and acts as a placeholder that renders the matched component for the current route.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: router-view in a Vue component template: `
`
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a <router-view> element in its template, ready to display routed components.
successCriteria: The App component template contains a <router-view> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the <router-view> element inside the App component's template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component template still needs a <router-view> element. Check that you've added it correctly.

steps.title: Add navigation links with router-link
steps.instruction: In the App component template, add two router-link elements inside the div: one for 'Home' that links to '/' and one for 'About' that links to '/about'.
steps.hint: Use the router-link component with the 'to' attribute to create navigation links. Place them before the router-view.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component template now includes navigation links that will allow users to switch between the Home and About pages.
successCriteria: Two router-link elements are added to the App component template with correct 'to' attributes ('/' and '/about') and appropriate text labels.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some navigation links, but check that you have both Home and About links with correct 'to' attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation links aren't properly configured. Make sure you're using router-link components with 'to' attributes pointing to '/' and '/about'.

steps.title: Initialize Vue with router
steps.instruction: Create a new Vue instance that uses the router and mounts to the DOM.
steps.hint: Use the Vue constructor with the router option and call the $mount method on the instance.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue instance is created with the router and mounted to the DOM.
successCriteria: The Vue instance uses the router and calls $mount.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're creating a Vue instance with the router option and mounting it.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a Vue instance that uses the router and mounts it.

steps.title: Test navigation between routes
steps.instruction: Click the 'Home' and 'About' navigation links to see the Home and About components render in the router-view area.
steps.hint: Click on each router-link element in the browser preview to navigate between routes and verify the content changes.

steps.expectedOutcome: When you click the 'Home' link, you should see 'Home Page' displayed. When you click the 'About' link, you should see 'About Page' displayed.
successCriteria: Clicking the navigation links successfully changes the displayed content between Home and About components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've partially completed the testing. Make sure you click both the 'Home' and 'About' links to verify both components render correctly.
